words.sentence: Chapter 1 covers legal requirements for new residents establishing residency, minor permit affidavits, licensing classifications, testing procedures, and mandatory address change timelines.

Chapter 6 explains Colorado's Express Consent Law, Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) thresholds for Driving Under the Influence (DUI) and Driving While Ability Impaired (DWAI) across age groups, cannabis impairment laws, construction zone fine doubling, and penalties for eluding law enforcement.

Chapter 5 explores regulations regarding school buses, commercial truck blind spots (No-Zones and Commercial Driver License (CDL) requirements), bicycle clearance, railroad crossings, and rural driving hazards.
Driving While Ability Impaired (DWAI) is a Colorado traffic charge triggered at a BAC of 0.05% where alcohol visibly affects faculties.
Avoid sudden braking during hydroplaning; easing off the gas allows tires to reestablish contact with the pavement.
Defensive Driving is a set of skills allowing motorists to guard against potential collisions from errors or road conditions.
A flashing yellow arrow requires you to yield right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.
Unless otherwise posted, the statutory speed limit in a Colorado urban residential district is 25 mph.
Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the weight amount of alcohol in blood volume, used as a legal metric for intoxication.
Brake Fade is the temporary loss of braking efficiency from excessive heat, common on steep mountain descents.
An Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup and maintains directional steering during emergency stops.
No-Zones are large blind spots in front, behind, and on both sides of commercial trucks where operators cannot see traffic.
Colorado enforces an Underage Drinking and Driving (UDD) limit of 0.02% Blood Alcohol Concentration for drivers under 21.
Driving Under the Influence (DUI) is applied when a motorist operates a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.
Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight specified by a manufacturer, determining license classification.
